about: Declares what it takes to move between released versions of DockVault. Every release must appear here before it can be cut; the release workflow refuses otherwise. Edges are declared between ADJACENT releases only -- a longer upgrade is composed by walking them in order, rather than being asserted as a single hop nobody tested.

kinds.direct: The upgrade can be taken in one step. Any caveats are listed in the edge's conditions.
kinds.blocked: The upgrade must not be taken. The edge says why, and what to do instead.

0.10.0.notes: No schema change. Every release up to here shares one physical schema: the set of boot DDL statements is byte-identical across all of them, and the model differs only in comment text.

0.11.0.notes: First release to change the physical schema: adds the vault_storage_grants table and a nullable users.storage_quota_bytes column, applied automatically and idempotently at boot. The additions are unused by 0.10.0, so a rollback is clean; take a backup before upgrading.

0.11.1.notes: No schema change; same physical schema as 0.11.0. Security patch: user-controlled values (the failed-login redis key and the alert resolver) are sanitized before they reach the security-monitor logs (log-injection hardening). A rollback is clean and needs no backup.

0.11.2.notes: No schema change; same physical schema as 0.11.0/0.11.1. Security hardening: closes a temporary-credential mint vault-password oracle (vault membership is now verified before the password proof), audits admin-plane and cross-tenant access denials, bounds client-supplied encrypted-name metadata, orders the user-update authorization check before the existence lookup, and re-checks temporary-credential deactivation on the web path every request. A rollback is clean and needs no backup.

0.12.0.notes: No schema change; same physical schema as 0.11.0/0.11.1/0.11.2. Adds credential lock/unlock/change-passphrase plus start/stop/restart/status lifecycle commands to the dockvault.py host management tool, so an operator can seal the .env secrets file into an encrypted .env.enc while a deployment is off (envelope encryption: a Fernet data key wrapped under a scrypt-derived passphrase key, with a stable recovery key). This is a host-tool change only; the container image is functionally unchanged from 0.11.2. Also hardens the test suite. A rollback is clean and needs no backup.

0.13.0.notes: Account onboarding. Adds two tables (account_invitations, email_change_codes), created automatically and idempotently at boot by create_all; both are additive and unused by 0.12.0, so a rollback is clean -- take a backup before upgrading. Verified live: a 0.12.0 stack upgraded to 0.13.0 over the same volume creates both tables (schema complete) and self-signup works. Features: admin account invitations (mint / list / revoke, plus a public single-use accept link); public self-signup gated by an org policy (email requirement, signup domain allow/deny, login identifier username/email/either); self-service email change with an emailed one-time verification code; a last-admin-email lockout guard; and log-access fixes (web log-pull in the split-container shape plus a settings-tab overflow fix).

0.14.0.notes: Adds six additive tables (email_profiles, email_templates, email_resources for the Email Studio; notifications; notes; email_actions), all created automatically and idempotently at boot by create_all and unused by 0.13.0, so a rollback is clean -- take a backup before upgrading. Features: Email Studio (branded HTML email templates with grouped substitution tokens and automated-email actions that route the verification-code / password-reset / invitation emails through the template mechanism, with a fail-safe that never sends a system security email missing its code or link token); an in-app notification bell plus a reworked three-lane non-admin dashboard (What's waiting for you / Favourites / Most recent); move and copy for files and folders, within a vault and across Standard vaults (re-encrypting content under the destination binding; zero-knowledge cross-vault deferred); personal server-side notes with a snapshot 'send note' to other users; and a rate-limiter split giving per-chunk uploads and polled reads their own generous budgets so large uploads and normal polling are no longer throttled.

0.15.0.notes: Public note links + notes UX. Adds two additive tables (note_link_tags, note_public_links), created automatically and idempotently at boot by create_all and unused by 0.14.0, so a rollback is clean -- take a backup before upgrading. Features: public note links -- a note owner can turn a note into an anonymous, tokenized SNAPSHOT link that anyone holding the link can read without signing in, governed by admin-defined 'note-link tags' that act as a security FLOOR the creator may only tighten (a longer token, an added or stronger PIN/password, a shorter expiry, fewer views), with anonymous redemption rate-limited per link, a per-link lockout after repeated wrong secrets, and fail-closed behaviour. Plus a Notes read modal with a left rail; clickable note tiles with wrapping text and bottom-aligned actions; a Send->Share chooser (send a copy to a member, or create a public link); a 'Shared (by me)' tab; live in-app notification delivery over the activity socket so a sent note appears without a page refresh (the socket now persists app-wide and re-checks session revocation); and admin oversight of every public link (list, revoke, and bulk-revoke). Host tool only: dockvault.py setup on a re-run now honours --image-source build so an operator can run freshly-pulled source instead of re-pulling the pinned release.

0.16.0.notes: Email templates & automation, plus notes-UX fixes. Schema: one additive nullable column, email_templates.default_key (created by create_all on a fresh DB, and by the boot DDL ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS on an existing one), plus a partial-unique index over it -- marks a template as the built-in default for an automated-email action; boot seeds a default template per action and pre-binds each action to its default (idempotent, never overwriting an admin's own template or 'none' choice). Two additive tables: otp_codes (the durable fallback for a generalized one-time-code service -- codes live in Redis first, this table when Redis is down; it supersedes email_change_codes, which is retained but no longer written) and password_reset_tokens (single-use, hashed-at-rest tokens for self-service and admin-triggered password-reset links). All additive and unused by 0.15.0, so a rollback is clean -- take a backup before upgrading. Features: a generalized OTP service backing email verification and password reset; self-service + admin-triggered password reset via emailed links; default email templates seeded with 'Load from default' in the Email Studio; and log redaction of sensitive values. Also folds in notes follow-up fixes: the sidebar no longer collapses when a very long note is present; the public-link creator gains a working Done button and disables 'never expires' under a lifetime-capped tag; the Shared tab refreshes live and can view a link's frozen snapshot; the active Notes tab persists across reload; a My-notes count badge; and a new admin 'maximum note size' setting.
